name: Agamaggan's Strength
summary: In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde travelers strength drawn from Blood Shards. The captive Razormane shaman honors the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan and hates the rival Bristleback tribe.

sections.title: Power of the Great Boar
sections.body: Quilboar honor Agamaggan, an ancient boar demigod. They say his spilled blood formed the red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. The crystals are sacred to them, and their power strengthens the fighters who stand at the front. Mangletooth, an elder Razormane shaman held captive in Camp Taurajo, offers that strength to Horde champions. He says your foes will cower before you as they do before the mightiest Razormane champions.

sections.title: A Bitter Shaman's Vengeance
sections.body: Mangletooth offers his strength out of spite. Orcs and tauren captured and caged the old quilboar, whose Razormane tribe is at war with the rival Bristleback. He cannot break his chains and slaughter them himself, so he trades Agamaggan's gifts for help against them. Those who destroy Bristleback tribes and take the sacred Blood Shards from their lands earn his blessing.

faq.answer: Agamaggan's Strength lends the recipient greater physical might through the power of Blood Shards. It grants the brutal strength of the fiercest Razormane fighters.
Mangletooth is an imprisoned Razormane quilboar held in Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens. He hates the rival Bristleback and trades quilboar secrets and blessings for Blood Shards.

aliases: where do blood shards come from
faq.answer: Blood Shards are reddish, crystal-like minerals found across the Barrens. Quilboar tradition says they formed where the blood of their patron demigod, the Great Boar Agamaggan, fell during the ancient War of the Ancients.

faq.q: Why does Mangletooth help the Horde?
faq.answer: Mangletooth helps the Horde because he hates the rival Bristleback quilboar. Caged at Camp Taurajo and abandoned by his own people, he grants Horde champions Agamaggan's blessings if they butcher his rivals and take their sacred Blood Shards.

faq.q: Can you receive this blessing more than once?
faq.answer: Yes. After your first trial for Mangletooth, he continues to weave Agamaggan's Strength and other boons when you bring him four more Blood Shards.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Bristleback and Razormane tribes?
faq.answer: The Bristleback and Razormane are rival quilboar tribes competing for the Barrens. Mangletooth belongs to the Razormane, despises the Bristleback, and boasts that his tribe is stronger.

angles.text: As a warrior, you draw on the raw vigor Mangletooth channels from the boar-god for a physical edge in battle across Kalimdor.
Camp Taurajo's guards keep Mangletooth locked up, but Horde commanders use the old shaman's thirst for vengeance against hostile quilboar.

As a tauren, you help maintain Camp Taurajo and watch Mangletooth warily. Your shamans recognize Agamaggan as an ancient guardian spirit of the land, though quilboar zealotry has corrupted his memory.
